channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: Black Friday price history: how to check if a deal is real
item.description: A Black Friday discount is only as real as the price it's compared with, and price history tools on Amazon, in Google Chrome and on price tracking sites show what an item actually cost in the past months.

item.title: Password manager hacked: what a breach can and can't expose
item.description: When a password manager company is hacked, your saved passwords stay locked as long as the vault is encrypted with a key only you hold, but your name, email and other account details can still leak and lead to targeted phishing.

item.title: Windows 11 slow performance fix: Microsoft's own tips explained
item.description: A slow Windows 11 PC is most often held back by apps that start with Windows, a nearly full drive, missing updates or background apps, and Microsoft's support page walks through switching each of them off.

item.title: Fake delivery scam: 54 fake couriers send tracking for parcels never sent
item.description: Fake online shops are giving buyers real-looking tracking numbers from made-up courier companies, so the order seems to be on its way while nothing was ever shipped. NordVPN's researchers found a network of 54 such fake couriers, most of them run from China.

item.title: 37 Shades of Late puts bus and train times on your iPhone Lock Screen
item.description: 37 Shades of Late is a new 99-cent iPhone app that shows the next buses, trains and ferries at your stop as minutes in Lock Screen and Home Screen widgets. It covers San Francisco, Seattle, New York, Boston, Chicago, Washington, D.C. and Los Angeles.

item.title: A Life in the Making: a self reflection journal app for iPhone
item.description: A Life in the Making is a $4.99 iPhone app with guided self reflection exercises on your values, your story, your thoughts and your relationships, and you don't need an account. It was #92 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Android 17 may keep audio in headphones when a car connects
item.description: A hidden "Keep audio in headphones" setting in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4, found by Android Authority, would stop sound from jumping to a car stereo or Bluetooth speaker when it connects. Google hasn't announced it, and it may not ship.

item.title: Calc89 graphing calculator app for iPhone with 89-style keys
item.description: Calc89 is a computer-algebra graphing calculator for iPhone and iPad laid out like the classic 89-style calculator keyboard, so known keystrokes work the same way. It costs $2.99 and was #80 in paid Education apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Capture. Focus. Reset. is a calm daily planner app for iPhone
item.description: Capture. Focus. Reset. is a new 3-dollar iPhone and iPad app for planning your day: you pick the few priorities that matter and leave the rest on a master list. Each day ends with a short review and a plan for tomorrow.

item.title: ChatGPT usage limits run out faster on GPT-6.2 after a billing fix
item.description: ChatGPT usage limits now run out about 40% faster with GPT-6.2 Astra and about 25% faster with GPT-6.2 Sol than last week, because OpenAI fixed a launch mistake that had counted these models' usage at a discount. Go, Plus, Pro and Business subscribers get one extra usage reset in return.

item.title: Chirpy Weather: AI weather app for iPhone you can ask questions
item.description: Chirpy Weather answers plain questions such as whether it will rain before evening, and builds a plan around the forecast for a run, a commute or a weekend trip: when to leave, what to bring, whether to move it. It's free with in-app purchases and was #87 among free Weather apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Claude Google Drive file browser spotted in testing
item.description: Anthropic is building a way to browse, search and filter your Google Docs, Sheets and Slides without leaving Claude, according to TestingCatalog, which shared screenshots dated 25 November. Anthropic hasn't announced it.

item.title: Facebook wallpaper ads spread malware that reads Gmail and Outlook
item.description: Fake ads on Facebook for free animated wallpapers install malware that makes Chrome, Edge or Firefox show "managed by your organization" and adds an extension that can read your email. Bitdefender calls the campaign SYS010.

item.title: Fold counter for iPhone Duo: Crease Control counts every hinge fold
item.description: Crease Control: Fold Odometer, a $0.99 app for foldable iPhones, keeps a running count of how often your phone has been folded, shown as a car-style odometer. It was #13 among paid Utilities apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Galaxy AI privacy: Samsung private cloud spotted in One UI 9.5 code
item.description: Code in the One UI 9.5 beta shows Samsung building a system called SPAC that would send Galaxy AI requests to its servers without showing who sent them, Android Authority found. Samsung hasn't announced it or said anything about it.

item.title: Gemini Chrome memory use: Google says the high RAM issue is fixed
item.description: Google's support account said on Reddit that the Gemini web app's high memory use in Chrome is resolved, Android Authority reported on 26 November. Users had complained about it for over a year, with one recent screenshot showing more than 5 GB of RAM.

item.title: HopFinder is a Space-A travel app for military flight schedules
item.description: HopFinder collects Space-A flight schedules from military AMC passenger terminals around the world in one iPhone and iPad app for retirees, veterans, service members and their families. It came out on 24 November for $3.99 and was #37 in paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: iPhone 20 Pro ceramic rumor points to a limited edition
item.description: Leaker Fixed Focus Digital says on Weibo they have ceramic parts for Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone, expected in fall 2027, and that very few will be made, which suggests a limited edition. Apple hasn't confirmed it, and the leaker didn't say which parts are ceramic.

item.title: Keycap: a mechanical keyboard look for the iPhone keyboard
item.description: Keycap is a 99-cent keyboard app for iPhone that draws the keys as raised caps with metal edges and a backlight that moves as you tilt the phone. It was #53 among paid Utilities apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Now Nudge on Samsung S26 tests suggestions for text you select
item.description: A hidden mode called Proactive Assistance in the One UI 9.5 beta for the Galaxy S26 series offers to call a number, add a date to your calendar or open directions when you type or select text, SamMobile found. It's switched off, and Samsung hasn't announced it.

item.title: Nuke Keyboard: new iPhone keyboard app with on-device dictation
item.description: Nuke Keyboard is a $4.99 iPhone keyboard with autocorrect, grammar fixes and dictation that run on the phone. It came out on 25 November and was #96 in paid Utilities on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Offline navigation app DeadZone maps hikes and trips without signal
item.description: DeadZone: Offline Navigation, a $3.99 iPhone and iPad app, lets you download maps and track your route where there's no cell coverage, for hiking, cycling, hunting, camping and off-road trips. It was #56 among paid Navigation apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Paint Jobs: painting estimate app for quotes and invoices on iPhone
item.description: Paint Jobs keeps a painter's customers, job photos, estimates and PDF invoices in one iPhone and iPad app for a one-time $9.99, with no subscription and no account. It came out on 25 November and was #29 in paid Business apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Passing Gas: fuel cost per mile app compares gas grades and E15
item.description: Passing Gas compares fuel grades, ethanol blends and pump prices by what they cost per mile instead of per gallon, including Unleaded 88 (E15). The $1.99 iPhone and iPad app by David McGuigan was #81 among paid Utilities apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Pit Stop: a bathroom finder app for iPhone that ranks nearby restrooms
item.description: Pit Stop finds public restrooms near you or any address and sorts them by walking or driving time, whether they're open now and how clean other users rate them. The 99-cent app was #87 among paid Navigation apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Quick Share Private sharing shutting down on Samsung Galaxy phones
item.description: Samsung is ending Private sharing in Quick Share, the mode for sending protected files between Galaxy devices. A notice in Quick Share version 13.9.10.5 on the Galaxy Store announces it, and the option is already missing in One UI 9.5 Beta 1.

item.title: Riemann hypothesis proof explained: how the Lean proof was verified
item.description: A proof of the Riemann hypothesis that Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he found working with Claude was checked line by line by computer programs within a day, but the official prize still needs a published paper, two years and the agreement of mathematicians.

item.title: Samsung Recompose may let Galaxy AI change a photo's angle
item.description: Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1's Photo Editor shows a Galaxy AI tool called Recompose that would let you change a photo's angle and perspective after you've taken it, Android Authority found. Samsung hasn't announced it, and it may not ship.

item.title: Second Look: a back seat reminder app for parents after every drive
item.description: Second Look Reminder is a $4.99 iPhone app that notices when you've been driving and reminds you to check your car after the trip. It was #94 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Send photos from iPhone to Mac with a flick: new app Zas
item.description: Zas sends a photo from your iPhone to your Mac when you press, hold and drag it to the top edge of the screen. The $2.99 app came out on 20 November and was #54 in paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Sidewalk Joy map app: find free little art galleries and swaps near you
item.description: Sidewalk Joy is a free iPhone and iPad app with a worldwide map of free street exchanges, such as little art galleries, trinket swaps, mug exchanges, puzzle libraries and seed swaps. It came out on 24 November and was #79 among free Navigation apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: TTStickers: WhatsApp sticker maker turns videos into animated stickers
item.description: TTStickers is a free iPhone and iPad app that turns your videos and photos into animated or still stickers and adds them to WhatsApp. It came out on 18 November and was #75 in free Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: Uber safety features for riders explained: PIN, recording, teens
item.description: Uber's app already has a ride PIN, trip sharing, crash and detour checks and audio recording for every rider, and in November 2026 it started testing video-recorded rides and rides for children as young as 10 in a few US cities.

item.title: USB port with a battery symbol: what it means and how to turn it off
item.description: A small battery or lightning bolt next to a laptop's USB port usually marks a port that can charge your phone or earbuds, on some laptops even while the lid is closed or the laptop is off.

item.title: Vivaldi adds Kagi search on Android in new Snapshot builds
item.description: Vivaldi Snapshot 4242.14 for Android, a preview build out on 25 November, adds Kagi Private Search as a search engine choice; Kagi is ad-free but paid after a free trial, and PiunikaWeb says the first 100 searches are free. The desktop Snapshot 4244.3 adds a command that takes you back to the workspace you used last.

item.title: WhatsApp eSIM for travel: buy a data plan in the app, coming soon
item.description: WhatsApp says you'll soon be able to buy and install a travel data eSIM inside the app and keep your WhatsApp number abroad. It announced this on 26 November with partners including Jio, Smart Axiata, Smart Communications and Verizon.

item.title: WorryTime worry journal app lets you park a thought for later
item.description: WorryTime is a 1-dollar iPhone app where you write down a worry in a few words and come back to it at a daily worry time you choose. Your notes stay on your iPhone.

item.title: YouTube TV Sports + News plan price: $49.99 a month for 6 months
item.description: New YouTube TV users in the US can get the Sports + News plan for $49.99 a month for their first 6 months, then $71.99 a month. YouTube's page says the offer ends on 2 December.

item.title: 1Password hacked: names and emails taken, passwords and vaults safe
item.description: 1Password says an attacker got into an employee's work GitHub account on 19 November and downloaded account records for some customers, including names and email addresses. Vault contents, the keys that protect them and recovery keys weren't accessed.

item.title: Adobe Acrobat Chrome extension linked to heavy SSD writes on a Windows PC
item.description: A Reddit user found Chrome had written over 300GB in about three days on a mostly idle Windows 11 PC and traced it to the Adobe Acrobat extension; after removing it, idle writes dropped by more than 81%.

item.title: Cam-Cord: iPhone camera app that saves the video before your photo
item.description: Cam-Cord starts recording when you tap once and takes the photo when you tap again, then saves a short clip of the seconds before the shot that ends on a freeze-frame of the photo. The $2.99 iPhone app came out on 25 November and was #32 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 26 November.

item.title: CardKeeper: business card scanner app for iPhone, no account
item.description: CardKeeper scans the front and back of a business card, reads the details on your iPhone and keeps both sides together with your notes. The $0.99 app came out on 24 November and was #38 among paid Business apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Carry saves ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok chats as Markdown files
item.description: Carry is a Chrome and Edge extension that backs up your chats, projects and files from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok as Markdown files in a folder you pick on your computer. You can search the saved chats and continue one in another AI.

item.title: ChangeLens Earth: satellite before and after app for any place
item.description: ChangeLens Earth lets you pick any place and two dates, then drag a divider across free satellite images to see what changed, from a new neighborhood to a shrinking glacier. The $0.99 iPhone and iPad app was #54 among paid Navigation apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: ChatGPT Health on Android now reads Health Connect and wearable data
item.description: OpenAI is rolling out ChatGPT Health on Android with Health Connect, so adults in the US can link watches and rings such as Garmin or Oura and ask about their steps and sleep. It works on the Free, Go, Plus and Pro plans and reaches accounts gradually.

item.title: ChatGPT usage limits: Chat and Work now share one meter
item.description: OpenAI has started merging ChatGPT's Chat and Work into one place with a single usage allowance, beginning with a small group of Pro subscribers on 25 November. Its help page says Plus, Pro and Business plans share one allowance across ChatGPT and Codex from December.

item.title: Claude Opus 5.6 rumors: testers say Anthropic is trying a new model
item.description: Some Claude users on X say their chats were answered by an unannounced model they call Opus 5.6, according to posts gathered by TestingCatalog on 24 and 25 November. Anthropic hasn't announced or confirmed it.

item.title: Cloud identification app Cielo names cloud types from your camera
item.description: Cielo, a $3.99 iPhone and iPad app, estimates which type of cloud is in the sky from your live camera, a photo or a saved video. It was #35 among paid Weather apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Cue by Manus: AI assistant app that books, orders and plans for you
item.description: Cue, an iPhone app from Manus maker Butterfly Effect, is an AI helper that can use apps you allow to plan trips, order food and book things, with you confirming each payment. It was #97 among free Productivity apps on the US App Store on 25 November.

item.title: Deevo prayer journal app for iPhone keeps entries on your phone
item.description: Deevo is a devotional journal for prayer, Scripture and reflection, with guided templates, prayer lists and an offline King James Bible. The $1.99 iPhone app came out on 23 November and was #95 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 25 November.
